subject.title: /acp sessions exposes every gateway ACP session to any allowlisted non-owner sender

question: Should `/acp sessions` be fixed by preserving documented non-owner access with requester-scoped results, or by making the command owner/admin-only as an immediate fail-closed hotfix?
rationale: Both paths close the data exposure, but they have different compatibility and UX tradeoffs for authorized non-owner diagnostics, so security-boundary intent should be explicit before implementation lands.

options.title: Scope non-owner results
options.body: Preserve the documented non-owner command by adding sender/session/account scoping to the listing path and regression coverage for a two-session cross-sender case.

options.title: Owner-gate sessions now
options.body: Move `sessions` into the owner/admin-required ACP action set and update docs/tests, accepting that authorized non-owners lose this diagnostic command.

options.title: Keep gateway-wide visibility
options.body: Only choose this if maintainers intentionally redefine `/acp sessions` as an owner/admin diagnostic and update the public contract accordingly.

recommendation.title: Scope non-owner results
recommendation.body: Preserve the documented non-owner command by adding sender/session/account scoping to the listing path and regression coverage for a two-session cross-sender case.

likelyOwner.reason: He carried the ACP command/session metadata feature history and is the strongest available owner for the intended requester-scoping model.
